title: "Inside double quotes, the shell replaces the $ of an R call"
ref: ENV-01
categories: [OS and CI]

attendu: "the path of the {renv} cache"
versions: "All, in bash, zsh and CI shells"

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```bash
Rscript -e "renv::paths$cache()"
```

```text
Error: attempt to apply non-function
Execution halted
```
:::

This pitfall depends on the shell that launches R, so it cannot be replayed in the browser.

## Why

Inside double quotes, the shell replaces `$cache` with the value of the `cache` environment variable, usually empty. R therefore receives `renv::paths()`. But `renv::paths` is not a function, it is a list of functions: calling it fails, with a message that says nothing about the vanished `$`.

The same pitfall hits `df$column`, `x$y` or a regular expression ending in `$` in a CI script.

## The remedy

Put the R code inside single quotes, which the shell leaves alone, and keep double quotes for use inside the R code.

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```bash
Rscript -e 'renv::paths$cache()'
```
:::
